C0.quote: We revisit the recent breakthrough result of Gkatzelis et al. on (single-winner) metric voting

C1.quote: The canonical voting rule we propose for electing from the (plurality) veto core also satisfies resolvability, monotonicity, majority, majority loser, mutual majority and reversal symmetry, in addition to still guaranteeing metric distortion 3.
C1.note: Primary type is axiomatic because the main results characterize the veto core and establish axioms; distortion (WD) is also central.

C2.1.quote: The vector of all rankings is referred to as a ranked-choice profile

C2.2.quote: let ≻v be a ranking (i.e., total order) over C

C2.3.quote: For each voter v, let ≻v be a ranking
C2.3.note: The paper refers to voters' rankings as held preferences.

C2.4.quote: the rankings provide ordinal information about the distances
C2.4.note: The rule is applied directly to the ranked-choice profile, which is treated as a held attitude; no separate submission object or statement that submitted input equals held attitude is given.

C3.1.quote: we currently do not know whether a stronger version holds
C3.1.note: No analysis models voters submitting an input that differs from their held attitude; the paper studies rules axiomatically and via distortion.

C3.2.loc: Introduction, p.1-2; Preliminaries, p.6-7; Conclusion, p.21-22
C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitude is found in the main text.

C4.1.quote: the distance between a voter and a candidate captures how much the voter dislikes the candidate
C4.1.note: Utilities/cost are linked to distances, which are consistent with rankings; social cost under a metric is defined.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: The (utilitarian) social cost of a candidate c under a metric d is defined as the total distance of voters to c
C5.1.note: Social welfare and distortion are used in results.

C5.2.quote: The distortion of a candidate c in an election E... is the largest possible ratio... with respect to a metric d
C5.2.note: The metric space serves as the held attitude, and outcomes are evaluated against it.

VOT.note: Voters are modelled as having fixed rankings; no strategic behaviour is analysed.

C7.1.note: Fewer than two types present by the C6 definition.

C8.1.note: No type is STRAT or MIXED; C8.1 is NA.

claims.quote: the canonical voting rule we propose... satisfies... resolvability, monotonicity, majority, majority loser, mutual majority and reversal symmetry, in addition to still guaranteeing metric distortion 3
this makes it well suited for practical adoption
a highly practical voting rule with optimal distortion 3

C9.2.note: Claims about distortion-3 performance require the metric to be consistent with rankings (stated), but claims about practicality (e.g., 'well suited for practical adoption') implicitly require that voters report rankings truthfully; the paper does not state this.

C10.1.quote: the voting rule does not have access to the actual distances; instead, the rankings provide ordinal information
C10.1.note: The paper explicitly states it studies the rule as a function of submitted rankings, not of cardinal distances.
